## Summary

**File modified:** `JavaSource/org/unitime/timetable/export/hql/SavedHqlExportToCSV.java`

### Modification
In the branch handling single-choice parameters (the `else` block for non-multi-select options), the patch wraps the existing logic inside a new `if (value != null)` check. Previously, the code unconditionally created an `IdValue` object, attempted to look up or parse the parameter value, and added it to the `params` list—even when `value` (obtained via `helper.getParameter(option.name())`) was `null`. This caused failures (e.g., NullPointerException or invalid entries) when exporting HQL reports as CSV for single-choice parameters such as SUBJECT or DEPARTMENT that had no value set.

The fix ensures that the `IdValue` creation, lookup, and parameter addition only occur when `value` is not `null`, effectively skipping parameters that have no value instead of processing them incorrectly.

### Relationship
This is a single, self-contained change within one file/method. The added null-check guards the parameter-processing logic (value lookup, numeric parsing, and addition to the `params` collection) so that it safely handles cases where a single-choice HQL report parameter has no corresponding value, preventing errors during CSV export.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
`String value = helper.getParameter(option.name());`
`Long id = option.lookupValue(context.getUser(), value);`
`params.add(v);`
Reason: For single-choice options, the code retrieves `value` via `helper.getParameter(option.name())` but does not check if it is `null` before using it. It unconditionally attempts to look up or parse `value` into an `IdValue` and adds it to `params`, even when the user never supplied a value for that parameter. This results in an invalid/empty `IdValue` being added to the parameter list whenever a single-choice parameter like SUBJECT or DEPARTMENT was not set, corrupting the parameters used to build the HQL query.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
`if (value != null) {`
`    ... (lookup, parsing, and params.add(v) logic moved inside this block)`
`}`
Reason: By wrapping the entire parameter construction and lookup logic inside a `null` check on `value`, the code now only creates and adds an `IdValue` to `params` when the user has actually supplied a value for the single-choice option. This prevents invalid or empty entries from being added to the parameter list when no value was set, ensuring the HQL query parameters are correctly built for CSV export.
